subject: Post-demo: performance deep-dive & SLO checklist
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Geller <sara.geller@solsticehealth.com>, Solstice Health Eng <eng@solsticehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: performance deep-dive & SLO checklist

Hi Sara / Tom / Eng team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great demo and very helpful context on the voice assistant workload. Per our discussion, I wanted to summarize the performance / SLO points we should align on and the immediate next steps for a short, instrumented trial. I attached a simple SLO checklist you can fill in.

Key customer targets we heard today (please confirm):
- Primary use case: real-time voice assistant (streaming responses) + fallback text-only flow.
- 95th percentile generation latency target (streaming end-to-end): <= 180 ms.
- 50th percentile latency (streaming): <= 70 ms.
- Sustained throughput target: 220 QPS across peak hours; burst capacity to 1,000 QPS for short events.
- Concurrent active sessions to support: ~600 concurrent streaming sessions with KV cache enabled; expected average tokens per request ~300.
- Quality constraint: model must preserve response fidelity for prompts with multi-turn context up to 2,000 tokens.

Immediate asks / dependencies from Solstice:
1) Confirm the above SLO numbers or provide a revised target (p95/p50, QPS, concurrency).
2) Share a representative prompt set and a 5-10 minute sample trace (we referenced sample-latency-traces-20270614.txt) so we can run offline simulations.
3) Confirm whether production will require Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) — that affects canary plan and benchmarking.

Redwood propose initial approach:
- Short 7-day load run in a sandbox (instrumented) to validate p95/p50 and throughput with a model variant tuned for latency (rwd-7b-quant).
- Canary configuration: dedicated pool (8 GPUs) + prefix/KV cache + streaming-optimized runtime; progressive ramping to target QPS.
- Metrics captured: per-token latency distribution, tail latencies (p90/p95/p99), queueing, GPU utilization, cold-starts, and generated-token counts.

Next steps (can we confirm by EOD Thursday?):
- You: confirm SLO numbers, share prompt set & traces, state deployment preference (Hosted vs Private).
- Us: return an explicit trial run plan with resource sizing, cost estimate, and a draft MAP (mutual action plan) for the trial.

Attachments: solstice-slo-checklist.xlsx (fillable), sample-latency-traces-20270614.txt (example).

Thanks — I’ll coordinate on Redwood side once you confirm.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

From: Sara Geller <sara.geller@solsticehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@solsticehealth.com>, Eng <eng@solsticehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance deep-dive & SLO checklist

Aditya —

Appreciate the quick recap. Confirming and adding detail from the Eng side:
- We validate the primary use case is streaming-first (voice assistant) with a text fallback.
- Target p95 generation latency (end-to-end streaming): <= 180 ms (keeping it tight is important for UX).
- Target p50: <= 65-75 ms depending on region; p99 target is less strict but should be monitored.
- Sustained throughput: 250 QPS (we prefer to plan for 15% headroom above expected load).
- Concurrency: 600 active streaming sessions; occasional bursts to 1,200 concurrent sessions are possible during marketing-driven peaks.
- Average tokens per request: 280-340; some long reports may bump sequences up to 1,500 tokens.

Operational notes:
- We will require Private deployment (VPC) for PHI-related traffic. That will affect how you provision canary infra and how we share traces.
- Security/compliance folks will want to see audit log config and key management options — happy to loop them in after we have a proposed trial plan.

Attached: an internal runbook excerpt (not attached here) and I’ll share a drive folder with the prompt set + a few sample traces today (expect link in a separate email).

Sara
Sara Geller
Head of Product, Platform | Solstice Health
sara.geller@solsticehealth.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Geller <sara.geller@solsticehealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance deep-dive & SLO checklist

On Wed, Jun 16, 2027 at 9:12 AM Sara Geller <sara.geller@solsticehealth.com> wrote:
> Aditya —
> 
> Appreciate the quick recap. Confirming and adding detail from the Eng side: ...

Thanks Sara — good clarity. A few notes from the SE perspective and proposed validation plan:

Proposed runtime/config for the trial (initial):
- Model variant: rwd-7b-quant (streaming-optimized); we can test rwd-13b-quant if you need higher fidelity.
- Dedicated pool suggestion: 8 x A5000-equivalent GPUs for steady-state; autoscale policy to add 4 GPUs at 15% increased queueing/latency.
- Runtime knobs: continuous batching window 10ms, KV cache TTL 30m for session affinity, prefix caching for repeated prompts.

Load test plan (7 days sandbox):
- Day 0: dry run with small prompt set + smoke checks, validate correctness.
- Day 1–3: ramp to 60% of target QPS and validate p50/p95 for streaming and non-streaming flows.
- Day 4–6: sustained run at 100% target QPS (250 QPS) with periodic bursts to 1,000 QPS. Capture p90/p95/p99 and queueing metrics.
- Day 7: soak + cleanup; compile report and recommendations (pool sizing / quantization changes / fallback models).

Data we need from Solstice to run the above:
- Representative prompt set (CSV or JSONL) and a few obfuscated traces (we got the example trace — thanks).
- A test account or API key (sandbox) and an IP allowlist for the Private deployment canary.

Risk notes:
- Private deployment adds ~48–72 hours to setup for network & KMS.
- If you have strict p99 constraints for certain flows we should flag them now; streaming tails can be sensitive to network jitter.

I’ll prepare a trial run plan and cost estimate and drop it into the shared Drive folder. If Solstice OKs, we can target starting the sandbox by June 28.

Action items for this thread:
- Sara/Tom: share prompt set + sandbox access window + confirm Private deployment requirement.
- Aditya: produce trial MAP and cost estimate.
- Monica (CS): prepare onboarding checklist and monitoring dashboard template.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Geller <sara.geller@solsticehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance deep-dive & SLO checklist

Adding a quick note from a GTM/ops perspective — thanks team, this looks on track.

Lauren’s quick decision-criteria checklist for the 7-day trial (please confirm):
- Acceptance criteria (must hit during sustained run at target QPS = 250):
  * p95 streaming latency <= 180 ms across two regions
  * p50 streaming latency <= 75 ms
  * No sustained GPU queueing (queue length < 5 requests for > 5 minutes)
  * 99% of requests return within the retry budget (no more than 1% errors)
- Security/compliance gating:
  * Private deployment + KMS integration validated in sandbox
  * Audit logs captured and accessible to Solstice compliance team
- Operational readiness:
  * Monitoring dashboard available with token-level and request-level breakdowns
  * Runbook for degraded-mode fallbacks (model variant fallback, region failover)

If we get confirmation from Solstice on the prompt set, the Private requirement, and a sandbox window this week, I approve we proceed with the 7-day trial and will sign off on the resource allocation.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
